title: The index is ODD at the prize, so the constant-index lane can never recurse via a 2-power head: F8 and F20 live on coprime-order sides of F_q*≅μ_n×ℤ/m
connection: prizeIndex_odd proves m=(q−1)/n is ODD when n=2^a is the full 2-part of q−1. The completion sum runs over t=m phases indexed by ℤ/m. A natural way to extract a constant head with cancellation is a 2-adic/parallelogram fold (F8: M(n)²≤2M(n/2)²) ON THE INDEX side — but doubling_bijective_of_odd shows x↦2x permutes ℤ/m (m odd), so Hasse–Davenport order-2 duplication gives NO 2-to-1 fold of the phase sequence. The dyadic descent F8 (which works on the SUBGROUP μ_n) is structurally unavailable on the INDEX group ℤ/m where the completion sum lives. F8 and F20 cannot be combined.
why_insightful: Links the proven parity fact to the constant-index lane's recursion barrier: people assume the dyadic structure powering F8 could recurse the phase DFT, but odd m forbids it — F8 and F20 live on coprime-order sides of F_q*≅μ_n×ℤ/m.
attack_plan: Lean: constIndex_no_dyadic_recursion combining prizeIndex_odd + doubling_bijective_of_odd to certify that any sub-√q saving in the m-phase completion sum must come from cancellation over an ODD-order cyclic group (no 2-adic tower), i.e. from Salem–Zygmund flatness over ℤ/m (F16), NOT F8. Documents why the 'fold the index by 2' attack is dead.
